name: issue_620_routine_classification_pauses_for_already_open_sensor
description: apply_classification()'s routine comfort-restore write must pause instead of setting an active HVAC mode when a monitored sensor has been open since before any event-driven pause path ever ran (Issue #620, Fix A)
notes: Occupant impact: on 2026-08-11, a door/window sensor had been open since bedtime (~05:25)
with no fresh 'sensor opened' event ever firing (handle_door_window_open() was never
invoked for it) -- so _paused_by_door stayed False. When the fan session that had been
suppressing HVAC ended, apply_classification()'s routine comfort-restore write went ahead
and set HVAC to cool@74F with the window open, because that write path only ever checked
the _paused_by_door FLAG (event history), never live sensor state.
Scenario design: outdoor is deliberately kept far above indoor throughout (85F vs 70F) so
nat-vent/WHF is never eligible or involved -- this isolates the routine
apply_classification() choke point (Fix A) from the nat-vent-specific fixes (B, C). The
sensor is seeded already-open (no dispatch), matching the real incident's shape of a
sensor that had been open for a while, not one that just opened. A second classification
event re-triggers apply_classification()'s routine write with the sensor already open --
this models any of the four real call sites (apply_classification/handle_bedtime/
handle_morning_wakeup/handle_pre_cool) re-evaluating on their next cycle.
Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md Sec 10):
(a) Scenario effectiveness: removing the
'await self._sync_paused_by_door_with_live_sensors()' call from
apply_classification() (Fix A) would make this scenario fail -- the second
classification event would proceed straight to PROCEED (whf_owns_hvac=False,
paused_by_door=False) and write cool@74F with the window open. Verified via
revert-test before promoting this scenario.
(b) Docs-production alignment: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md's
decide_scheduled_band_gate() / Issue #498 section is updated (Issue #620 doc pass) to
document _sync_paused_by_door_with_live_sensors() as the mechanism that keeps its
paused_by_door input truthful.
(c) User outcome: the home stays paused (HVAC off) instead of silently starting to cool
with a window open that automation never noticed was open.

events.note: Afternoon: indoor 70F, outdoor 85F -- outdoor well above indoor, nat-vent never eligible. Isolates the routine classification choke point from the nat-vent fixes.
First classification application: HVAC set to cool@74F normally (no sensor open yet).
Window already open, seeded silently (no dispatch) -- models a sensor that's been open for a while with no fresh open event, matching the real incident. handle_door_window_open() never runs for it.
Next classification cycle (models the 30-min re-evaluation) re-runs apply_classification() with the sensor now open. Must pause instead of re-affirming cool@74F.

assertions.reason: First classification applies normally -- no sensor open, nothing to pause for.

Issue #620 Fix A: apply_classification() must call _sync_paused_by_door_with_live_sensors() before building decide_scheduled_band_gate()'s inputs. With the sensor settled-open (seeded, past any debounce window) and no other guard (nat-vent/WHF/planned-window) claiming it, this must set _paused_by_door=True and defer the band -- not silently write cool@74F into the open window.

verdict.summary: Routine classification re-application pauses instead of writing an active mode when a sensor has been open since before any event-driven pause ever ran (Issue #620, Fix A)
verdict.observed_behavior: classification_applied (cool@74F, sensor closed) -> sensor opens (seeded, no dispatch) -> next classification cycle -> paused_by_door=True, HVAC deferred instead of re-affirmed
verdict.expected_behavior: A sensor open since before any pause-triggering event still blocks the routine comfort-restore write, exactly as if it had just been freshly detected open
